title: Steel Design
description: Comprehensive practice quiz covering all core topics of steel structure design as per IS:800 — Beams, Compression Members, Girders, Plastic Theory, Riveted & Bolted Connections, Steel (General), Tension Members, and Welded Connections.

questions.text: The members laid horizontally to support the common rafters and to transmit the load to the front walls are called as
questions.expl: Purlins are horizontal members that support common rafters and transfer roof loads to the walls/trusses.

questions.text: As per IS:800 WSM the maximum deflection in a beam should not exceed
questions.expl: Under the older Working Stress Method, IS:800 limited beam deflection to L/325.

questions.text: A beam is defined as a structural member subjected to
questions.expl: A beam primarily resists loads applied transverse (perpendicular) to its longitudinal axis, causing bending.

questions.text: A web plate is called unstiffened if the ratio of clear depth and thickness is less than
questions.expl: IS:800 permits an unstiffened web when d/t ratio is less than 85 (for grade Fe410 steel).

questions.text: As per IS:800, the maximum bending moment for design of purlins can be taken as
questions.expl: Purlins spanning over multiple supports are conventionally designed for a reduced moment of WL/10.

questions.text: Generally the purlins are placed at panel points so as to avoid
questions.expl: Placing purlins at panel (node) points ensures the rafter carries only axial force, avoiding bending moment.

questions.text: Normally the angle of roof truss with asbestos sheets should not be less than
questions.expl: A minimum slope of about 30° is recommended for asbestos cement sheet roofing to ensure proper drainage.

questions.text: The range of economical spacing of trusses varies from
questions.expl: For a truss of span L, economical spacing of trusses generally lies between L/3 and L/5.

questions.text: As per IS:800, the thickness of slab base is given by
questions.expl: The slab base thickness formula is derived from bending of the plate under bearing pressure: t = √[3W/Fb(A² − B²/4)].

questions.text: As per IS:800:2007, the maximum deflection in a beam should not exceed
questions.expl: Under the current Limit State Method (IS:800:2007), the deflection limit for beams carrying elastic cladding is L/300.

questions.text: A beam section is selected and provided on the basis of
questions.expl: Beam sizing must satisfy bending (section modulus), shear, and serviceability (deflection) requirements together.

questions.text: Match List-I and List-II: (i) Tie (ii) Boom (iii) Strut (iv) Joist with 1. Member supporting roof 2. Tension member in roof truss 3. Compression member in roof truss 4. Compression member in crane
questions.expl: Tie = tension member(2), Boom = compression member of crane(4), Strut = compression member of truss(3), Joist = roof-supporting member(1).

questions.text: As per IS specifications, the beam sections should be
options: At least symmetrical about one of the principal axes
Preferably plastic or compact sections only
Rolled to furnish maximum sectional modulus
questions.expl: IS:800 recommends beam sections to be symmetrical, compact/plastic, and efficient in providing section modulus.

questions.text: Beams should be designed and checked for
questions.expl: A complete beam design check covers bending (flexural) strength, deflection (stiffness), and local buckling of elements.

questions.text: Design of a beam is governed by shear
options: When the depth of beam section is small and the beam is loaded uniformly
When large concentrated loads are placed near beam supports
None of the above is correct
questions.expl: Shear governs design in short, heavily loaded beams and where large point loads act close to supports.

questions.text: Web crippling in steel beam occurs due to
options: Failure of web under concentrated load
questions.expl: Web crippling is a local bearing failure of the web directly under a concentrated load or at supports.

questions.text: The slenderness ratio of web of beam section from diagonal buckling consideration is given by
questions.expl: The effective slenderness ratio for diagonal (shear) buckling of the web is taken as 2.45 d/tw.

questions.text: Deflection limitations over beams are imposed because excessive deflection
options: May create problems for roof drainage
May cause undesirable twisting and distortion of end connections
May cause psychological problems for the users
questions.expl: Deflection limits control ponding/drainage issues, connection distress, and occupant discomfort, among other things.

questions.text: The lateral restraint at the supports for a laterally supported beam may be in the form of
questions.expl: Lateral restraint at supports can be achieved by web cleats, end plates, or continuity — any of these suffice.

questions.text: As per IS:800 purlins are designed as
questions.expl: Purlins spanning across several truss panels are usually designed as continuous beams over supports.

questions.text: Sag rods are designed as
questions.expl: Sag rods only resist the tendency of purlins to slide down the slope, so they act purely in tension.

questions.text: A beam section is classed as low shear case when the factored shear force is less than
questions.expl: As per IS:800, if factored shear force is ≤ 0.6 times the design shear strength (Vd), it is a low shear case.

questions.text: The design bending strength of a laterally supported beam is Md = βb·Zp·fy/γm0. βb for plastic, compact sections are given by
questions.expl: For both plastic and compact sections, βb = 1.0 since the full plastic moment capacity can be mobilized.

questions.text: The shear lag effect in beam flanges are disregarded when the outstand of the beam flange is less than or equal to
questions.expl: Shear lag in flanges can be ignored when the flange outstand does not exceed L0/20 (L0 = distance between points of zero moment).

questions.text: The design bending strength of a laterally unsupported beam is given by which formula(s)?
questions.expl: For laterally unsupported beams, Md = βbZpfbd or βbZpχLTfy/γm0, i.e. options 2 and 3, using the reduced bending stress fbd.

questions.text: The elastic lateral torsional buckling moment Mcr for laterally unsupported beams is given by
questions.expl: Mcr, the elastic critical moment, is expressed in terms of βb, Zp and the elastic critical bending stress fcr,b.

questions.text: I-section beams have
questions.expl: Open thin-walled I-sections have relatively low and comparable torsional and warping rigidities, making them prone to lateral torsional buckling.

questions.text: Beams with compact section attain plastic moment capacity due to
options: Possibility of sufficient plastic hinge rotation
questions.expl: Compact sections can reach full plastic moment because stresses redistribute plastically across the section before local buckling occurs.

questions.text: Compression members are generally called
questions.expl: A member subjected mainly to axial compressive force is generically termed a strut.

questions.text: An electric pole is 10 meter high from ground level, its effective length for the design will be
questions.expl: A pole fixed at base and free at top behaves as a cantilever, so effective length = 2L = 20 m.

questions.text: Effective length of a chimney of 20 m height shall be taken as
questions.expl: A chimney, fixed at base and free at top, is a cantilever column with effective length = 2 × 20 = 40 m.

questions.text: Lacings in the built up steel column are designed to resist
options: BM due to 2.5% of column load
SF due to 2.5% of column load
Axial force due to 2.5% of column load
questions.expl: Lacing systems must resist a transverse shear force equal to 2.5% of the total axial load in the column.

questions.text: The effective length of battened column is increased by
questions.expl: IS:800 requires the effective length of a battened column to be increased by 10% to account for reduced shear rigidity.

questions.text: The slenderness ratio of a column supported throughout its length by a masonry wall is
questions.expl: If a column is continuously restrained throughout its length, its effective length (and hence slenderness ratio) is taken as zero.

questions.text: According to IS specification, the effective length of a column effectively held in position at both ends and restrained in direction at one end is taken as
questions.expl: For one end fixed in direction and both ends held in position, IS:800 gives effective length as 0.80 L.

questions.text: The increase in effective length of column the slenderness ratio
questions.expl: Slenderness ratio = effective length / radius of gyration, so a larger effective length directly increases it.

questions.text: An electric pole is 5 m high and it is fixed to the ground. It carries a wire at the top, and is free to move sideways over there. The effective length of the pole is
questions.expl: Fixed at base and free (unrestrained) at top makes this a cantilever column, giving effective length = 2L = 10 m.

questions.text: ________ are the structural members that are subjected to external forces and moments.
questions.expl: Columns are compression members that must resist axial forces along with possible bending moments from eccentric loading.

questions.text: Maximum value of slenderness ratio of lacing flats in a steel column is:
questions.expl: IS:800 limits the slenderness ratio of lacing bars/flats to a maximum of 145.

questions.text: As per IS:800–1984, the lacings of compression member shall be proportioned to resist a total transverse shear 'S' equal to at least
questions.expl: Lacing systems in built-up compression members are designed for a minimum transverse shear of 2.5% of the axial load.

questions.text: As per codal provision, the effective buckling length of a cantilever steel column of length L is given by
questions.expl: A cantilever (fixed at base, free at top) column has effective length equal to 2L.

questions.text: Battens provided for a compression member shall be designed to carry a transverse shear equal to
questions.expl: Similar to lacing, battens are also designed for a minimum transverse shear of 2.5% of the axial force.

questions.text: Lug angles
options: Are used to reduce the length of the connection
questions.expl: Lug angles help transfer part of the load from the outstanding leg earlier, reducing the required connection length.

questions.text: The least dimension in case of a circular column of diameter D is taken as
questions.expl: For a solid circular column, the least radius of gyration corresponds to an effective 'least dimension' of about 0.88D (r = D/4, giving equivalent slenderness comparisons).

questions.text: The bracing provided in the plane of end posts is called
questions.expl: Portal bracing is provided in the vertical plane of the end posts of a truss to transfer lateral forces to the supports.

questions.text: As per IS:800, for compression flange, the outstand of flange plates should not exceed
questions.expl: The outstand of a compression flange plate is limited to 16 times its thickness to prevent local buckling.

questions.text: The overlap of batten plates with the main members in welded connections should be more than
questions.expl: In welded battened columns, the overlap of the batten with the main member should exceed 4 times the batten thickness.

questions.text: The effective length of a laced column is increased by
questions.expl: IS:800 requires only a small (5%) increase in effective length for laced columns, compared to 10% for battened columns.

questions.text: If the 20 mm rivets are used in lacing bars, then the minimum width of lacing bar should be
questions.expl: Minimum lacing bar width is generally taken as three times the rivet diameter, i.e. 3 × 20 = 60 mm.

questions.text: According to IS:800, in the Merchant Rankine's formula the value of imperfection index (n) is
questions.expl: IS:800 adopts the Perry-Robertson/Merchant-Rankine approach with an imperfection index n taken as 1.4.

questions.text: The maximum slenderness ratio of steel column, the design of which is governed by wind or seismic forces is
questions.expl: For compression members carrying loads resulting from wind/seismic forces only, the maximum permissible slenderness ratio is 250.

questions.text: The maximum slenderness ratio of a compression member carrying both dead and superimposed load is
questions.expl: A compression member carrying dead and live (superimposed) loads is limited to a slenderness ratio of 180.

questions.text: Which of the following section will be preferred for a column?
questions.expl: ISHB (Indian Standard Heavy Beam) sections have wider flanges and near-equal radii of gyration about both axes, making them best suited as columns.

questions.text: The most suitable compression member section for a roof truss is
options: Double angles placed back to back
questions.expl: Tubular sections have equal radius of gyration in all directions, making them the most efficient compression member shape.

questions.text: A column that can support same load in compression that it can in tension is classed as
questions.expl: A very short (stocky) column fails by yielding/crushing, so its capacity in compression equals its capacity in tension.

questions.text: Match List-I (Types of members) with List-II (Slenderness ratio): (i) dead & live loads (ii) wind/seismic compressive loads (iii) tension members with stress reversal due to wind/seismic
questions.expl: Dead+live loads → SR 180(2); wind/seismic compression → SR 250(3); tension with stress reversal → SR 350(1), matching option B.

questions.text: The effective length of a strut (double angle on opposite side of gusset plate) of actual length L, in a plane perpendicular to the gusset plate will be
questions.expl: For double angle struts connected on opposite sides of a gusset with adequate end connections, effective length in the perpendicular plane ranges from 0.7L to 0.85L.

questions.text: The slenderness ratio of a single-angle single bolted strut should be less than
questions.expl: A single-angle strut connected by a single bolt is treated as a dead/live load carrying compression member, limited to slenderness ratio 180.

questions.text: Splices for compression members are designed as
questions.expl: Column splices are conservatively designed treating the connection as a short column to transfer full compressive force safely.

questions.text: The effective length of a steel column effectively held in position at both ends and restrained in rotation at one end is
questions.expl: For both ends held in position, with one end restrained in direction (rotation), IS:800 gives effective length = 0.80L.

questions.text: The slenderness ratio of compression members is limited to account for
options: The effect of accidental and construction loads
They may be used as a walkway in braced roof truss system
questions.expl: Slenderness limits guard against accidental loads, serviceability during use as a walkway, and vibration issues, among other concerns.

questions.text: The design compressive stress of an axially loaded compression member in IS:800–2007 is given by
questions.expl: IS:800:2007 bases the design compressive stress (buckling curves) on the Perry-Robertson formula.

questions.text: Minimum number of battens required in a built up column are
questions.expl: A batten column requires a minimum of 3 batten plates along its length for stability, including battens near the ends.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a design criterion of a lattice column?
options: Buckling of the column as a whole
Buckling of the individual rolled sections constituting column
questions.expl: Lattice column design checks overall buckling, component (chord) buckling and lattice member buckling — not the buckling of individual rolled sections in isolation.

questions.text: Thickness of lacing flats for a single lacing system should not be less than
questions.expl: For a single lacing system, the flat's thickness must be at least 1/40th of its effective (span) length.

questions.text: For same load, unsupported length and end conditions, a laced column as compared to battened column
questions.expl: Lacing provides greater shear rigidity than battening, so a laced column is generally stronger for the same conditions.

questions.text: The distance between C.G. of compression flange and C.G. of tension flange of a plate girder is known as
questions.expl: Effective depth is measured between the centroids of the compression and tension flanges.

questions.text: Economical depth of the plate girder corresponds to minimum
questions.expl: The economical depth is that depth of girder which results in the minimum total weight (and hence cost) of steel.

questions.text: Bearing stiffener in plate girder are provided at
questions.expl: Bearing stiffeners are provided at supports and under concentrated loads to prevent web crippling/buckling from bearing stresses.

questions.text: Steel tanks are mainly designed for
questions.expl: The primary design load for a steel tank is the hydrostatic (water) pressure it must contain.

questions.text: Minimum pitch provided in riveted steel tanks is
questions.expl: For watertight riveted steel tank joints, a minimum pitch of 3 times the rivet diameter is specified.

questions.text: The number of seismic zones in which the country is divided are
questions.expl: As per IS:1893, India is divided into 4 seismic zones (Zone II to Zone V).

questions.text: Gantry girders are designed to resist
questions.expl: Gantry girders must be designed for the combined effect of vertical (wheel) loads, lateral (surge) loads and longitudinal (traction) loads.

questions.text: Economical depth of a plate girder is given by
questions.expl: The classical economical depth formula for a plate girder is approximately d = 1.1√(M/σtw).

questions.text: Intermediate vertical stiffeners are provided in plate girders to
questions.expl: Intermediate vertical stiffeners increase the shear buckling resistance of a slender web, preventing web (shear) buckling.

questions.text: The maximum span upto which plate girders can be used economically is
questions.expl: Plate girders are generally economical for spans up to about 40 m, beyond which trusses become more efficient.

questions.text: The vertical plate of a plate girder is termed as
questions.expl: The vertical plate that primarily resists shear in a plate girder is called the web plate.

questions.text: The girders having two or more than two webs are called
questions.expl: A girder fabricated with two (or more) webs connected by top and bottom flanges forming a closed/open box shape is a box girder.

questions.text: The horizontal plates connected with the flange angle are known as
questions.expl: The horizontal plates riveted/welded to the flange angles to increase flange area are called flange or cover plates.

questions.text: As compared to span, depth of plate girder is generally kept as
questions.expl: The depth of a plate girder is generally proportioned to about 1/10 to 1/12 of its span for economy.

questions.text: A girder is called shallow plate girder, if its depth is
questions.expl: A plate girder with a depth less than 75 cm is generally classified as a shallow girder.

questions.text: The thickness of web for unstiffened plate girder with clear distance d between the flange shall not be less than
questions.expl: For an unstiffened web (with both edges connected to flanges), minimum thickness is d/85 to control buckling.

questions.text: For large span and heavy gravity loads which of the following will be economical?
questions.expl: For large spans with heavy gravity loads, a plate girder is generally the more economical structural solution among these options.

questions.text: In a bolted plate girder flange, the angle section used should be
options: Unequal angle with long leg horizontal
Unequal angle with short leg horizontal
questions.expl: Unequal angles with the longer leg placed horizontally are preferred to maximize the flange's moment of inertia.

questions.text: As per IS:800 in the case of a plate girder with vertical and horizontal stiffeners, the greater and lesser unsupported clear dimension of a web panel in terms of web thickness tw should not exceed respectively
questions.expl: IS:800 limits the larger unsupported panel dimension to 270tw and the smaller to 200tw when both vertical and horizontal stiffeners are used.

questions.text: The optimum depth of plate girder is given by
questions.expl: As per limit state design, the optimum girder depth is given approximately by d = (Mk²/fy)^0.33.

questions.text: Vertical stiffeners in a bolted plate girder are
options: Placed alternately on both sides of web
Placed with a maximum spacing of 200 times thickness of web
questions.expl: Vertical stiffeners are typically crimped to fit the flange, placed alternately on both sides, and spaced within 200tw — all correct.

questions.text: The thickness of a web for unstiffened plate girder with clear distance d between the flanges, for serviceability requirement (web connected to flange along one longitudinal edge only) should not be less than
questions.expl: When the web is connected to a flange along only one edge (as in the case of a rail/crane girder), the serviceability limit is d/160.

questions.text: A length x of a web, on both sides of the web, acting as part of a bearing stiffener in compression is
questions.expl: IS:800 permits an effective web length of 20tw total (i.e., a length equal to 20tw, sometimes expressed as up to 20tw about the stiffener) to act with a bearing stiffener; option (B) 12tw corresponds to codal outstand-based value used here.

questions.text: The connection of vertical stiffener to the web of plate girder are designed for
questions.expl: The stiffener-to-web weld/connection is designed for a shear force proportional to tw²/(5bs), as per IS:800 provisions.

questions.text: End panel design of plate girder by post critical method
options: Makes use of tension field action
Avoids formation of tension field in the end panel
questions.expl: In the simple post-critical (non-tension-field) method for the end panel, tension field action is deliberately avoided for stability.

questions.text: Thick web of plate girder fails due to
questions.expl: A thick (stocky) web does not buckle in shear; instead it fails by shear yielding of the material.

questions.text: To prevent plate girders from being flexible normal to their web plane during fabrication and erection, following limit(s) is (are) placed by IS:800.
questions.expl: IS:800 restricts both the d/tw ratio (<270) and the panel aspect ratio c/d (<3) to control out-of-plane flexibility during handling.

questions.text: Which of the following loads are to be considered in designing a gantry girder in an industrial building?
questions.expl: Gantry girders must be designed for gravity, lateral, and longitudinal loads (1, 2 and 3) arising from crane operation.

questions.text: The function of the top channel in a crane girder is to
questions.expl: The top channel increases moment of inertia about the vertical axis, adds torsional stiffness, and improves lateral buckling strength (statements 1, 3, 4).

questions.text: Gantry girders are usually designed
options: For a combination of vertical loads and either of the lateral and longitudinal force
questions.expl: Gantry girders are typically laterally unsupported and must be checked for a combination of vertical loads with lateral or longitudinal forces.

questions.text: Gantry girders can be designed (1) and provided in multistory buildings (2) as laterally unsupported beams (3) using channel sections only
questions.expl: Only statement 2 is generally valid — gantry girders are usually designed as laterally unsupported beams; they aren't restricted to multistorey buildings or channel sections only.

questions.text: For gantry girders carrying electrically operated overhead traveling cranes, the lateral force are increased by
options: 10% of the weight of the crab and weight lifted by the crane
5% of the weight of the crab and weight lifted by the crane
questions.expl: The lateral (surge) force for EOT cranes is taken as 10% of the weight of the crab plus the load lifted.

questions.text: When gantry girders carry moving loads such as charging cars, the deflection should not exceed
questions.expl: For gantry girders subjected to loads from manually/electrically operated cranes such as charging cars, deflection is limited to L/600.

questions.text: The surge loads in gantry girders are
questions.expl: Surge load refers specifically to the lateral load generated by crane acceleration/braking, i.e., statement 2.

questions.text: Shape factor for a circular section is equal to:
questions.expl: For a solid circular section, the shape factor (Zp/Ze) is 16/(3π) ≈ 1.70.

questions.text: If the shape factor of a section is 1.5 and the factor of safety to be adopted is 2, then the load factor will be
questions.expl: Load factor = shape factor × factor of safety = 1.5 × 2 = 3.

questions.text: At the location of plastic hinge
questions.expl: At a plastic hinge, large rotation occurs at essentially constant moment, meaning curvature tends to infinity (radius of curvature tends to zero).

questions.text: In plastic analysis for flexure, which of the following pairs of shape of section and shape factor are not correctly matched?
questions.expl: The shape factor for an I-section is typically about 1.12–1.15, not 1.4, so this pairing is incorrect.

questions.text: The shape factor of an isosceles triangle for bending about the axis parallel to the base is:
questions.expl: For a triangular section bent about the axis parallel to its base, the shape factor works out to 2.34.

questions.text: The plastic section modulus for a rectangular section of width b and depth d is
questions.expl: The plastic section modulus of a rectangle is Zp = bd²/4, twice the elastic section modulus bd²/6.

questions.text: The shape factor for a solid circular section subjected to bending about its diameter
questions.expl: The shape factor of a solid circular section bent about a diameter is 16/(3π) ≈ 1.70.

questions.text: Which of the following sections will have large shape factor
questions.expl: A diamond (rhombus) section has material concentrated near the neutral axis, giving it the largest shape factor (~2.0) among these.

questions.text: Which one of the following conditions, both elastic and plastic methods of analysis of indeterminate structures have to satisfy?
questions.expl: Both elastic and plastic analyses must always satisfy static equilibrium, regardless of yield or compatibility assumptions.

questions.text: Consider the following statements: 1. Shape factor 2. Length of the beam 3. Type of loading 4. Yield strength of material. Which of these affect the influence length of plastic hinge in a beam?
questions.expl: The influence (spread) length of a plastic hinge depends on the shape factor of the section and the type of loading applied.

questions.text: Yield line theory results in
questions.expl: Yield line theory for slabs is based on the kinematic (mechanism) approach, which always gives an upper bound solution.

questions.text: In a plastic analysis of structures, the segment between any two successive plastic hinges is assumed to deform as
questions.expl: Between plastic hinges, the beam segments are assumed to remain rigid (undeformed), with all rotation concentrated at the hinges.

questions.text: What is the ratio of the shape factors for beam cross-sections having rectangular, circular and triangular shapes and of same area?
questions.expl: For equal-area sections, comparing shape factors of rectangle, circle and triangle gives approximately the ratio 1.00 : 1.13 : 1.56.

questions.text: Which one of the following is the correct ratio of plastic moment to yield moment for a simply supported beam of uniform square cross-section throughout the span?
questions.expl: The ratio of plastic moment to yield moment for a square section equals its shape factor, which is 1.5.

questions.text: In the virtual work method of plastic analysis of steel structure, the virtual quantity is
questions.expl: In the virtual work (mechanism) method of plastic analysis, a virtual displacement is imposed to equate external and internal work.

questions.text: Which of the following conditions is to be satisfied both in elastic and plastic analysis?
questions.expl: Static equilibrium is a fundamental requirement common to both elastic and plastic methods of structural analysis.

questions.text: The shape factors of a triangle section and a diamond section are respectively
questions.expl: A triangular section has shape factor 2.343, while a diamond (rhombus) section has shape factor 2.0.

questions.text: The perpendicular distance between the line of action of the load and centroid of the rivet group is called
questions.expl: Eccentricity is defined as the perpendicular distance between the load's line of action and the centroid of the rivet/bolt group.

questions.text: The thickness of gusset plate should not be less than
questions.expl: IS practice specifies a minimum gusset plate thickness of 6 mm.

questions.text: The maximum pitch of any two adjacent rivets in terms of thickness of plate 't' is limited to
questions.expl: The maximum pitch between adjacent rivets is limited to 32t (in compression) but generally quoted as 36t here for tension/compression combined checks depending on plate thickness class.

questions.text: If the thickness of the thinnest outside plate is 10 mm, then the maximum pitch in tension will be taken as
questions.expl: Maximum pitch in tension is the lesser of 16t (=160mm) or 200mm; per this answer key 200 mm governs for the outer plate check specified.

questions.text: The difference between gross diameter and nominal diameter of rivets up to 25 mm diameter is
questions.expl: For rivets up to 25 mm nominal diameter, the gross (hole) diameter exceeds nominal diameter by 1.5 mm.

questions.text: Efficiency of the riveted joint, having the minimum pitch as per IS:800, is
questions.expl: With the minimum permissible pitch, the net section is reduced enough that joint efficiency works out to about 60%.

questions.text: A rivet in a lap joint is in
questions.expl: In a lap joint, plates overlap and are connected by a single row of rivets, placing each rivet in single shear.

questions.text: Net sectional area of a tension member is equal to its gross section area
options: Plus the area of the rivet holes
Divided by the area of the rivet holes
Multiplied by the area of the rivet holes
Minus the area of the rivet holes
questions.expl: Net area is obtained by subtracting the area of rivet/bolt holes from the gross cross-sectional area.

questions.text: To the calculated area of cover plates of a built up beam, an allowance for rivet holes to be added is
questions.expl: A conventional allowance of about 10% extra area is added to cover plates of built-up beams to account for rivet holes.

questions.text: The maximum centre to centre distance between rivets in a tension member of thickness 10 mm is
questions.expl: Maximum pitch in tension members is limited to 16t = 16×10 = 160 mm.

questions.text: A riveted joint can fail in
options: Bearing of plate or rivet only
questions.expl: A riveted joint may fail by any of several modes: plate tearing, rivet shearing, or bearing failure of plate/rivet.

questions.text: The gross diameter of a 14 mm nominal diameter rivet is
questions.expl: For rivets up to 25 mm, gross diameter = nominal diameter + 1.5 mm = 14 + 1.5 = 15.5 mm.

questions.text: The strength of field rivets as compare to shop rivets is
questions.expl: Field-driven rivets are less reliably formed than shop rivets, so their strength is taken as only 75% of shop rivet strength.

questions.text: Bolts are most suitable to carry
questions.expl: Ordinary bolts are best suited for carrying axial tension, as they can be easily tightened to develop clamping/tensile capacity.

questions.text: Minimum thickness of main steel members, not exposed to weather, is:
questions.expl: IS:800 specifies a minimum thickness of 6 mm for main steel members not directly exposed to weathering.

questions.text: The size of the rivet is expressed by the
questions.expl: Rivet size is conventionally specified by the (nominal) diameter of its shank.

questions.text: Minimum pitch of rivets should not be less than how many times of gross diameter of rivet?
questions.expl: IS:800 specifies a minimum pitch of 2.5 times the gross diameter of the rivet.

questions.text: The gross diameter of rivet (hole) for a rivet with nominal diameter of 27 mm is
questions.expl: For rivets over 25 mm nominal diameter, gross diameter = nominal + 2 mm = 27 + 2 = 29 mm.

questions.text: The maximum permissible stress in shear for power driven shop rivet is
questions.expl: Under the working stress method, the permissible shear stress for power-driven shop rivets is 100 N/mm².

questions.text: Diameter of a rivet hole should be greater than the nominal diameter of rivet by about
questions.expl: The rivet hole diameter is drilled about 1.5 to 2 mm larger than the nominal rivet diameter to allow driving clearance.

questions.text: According to IS specifications, the maximum pitch of rivets in compression is
questions.expl: In compression members, the maximum pitch is limited to the lesser of 200 mm or 12 times the thickness of the thinnest outside plate.

questions.text: When the bolts are subjected to reversal of stresses, the most suitable type of bolt is
questions.expl: High strength friction grip (HSFG) bolts resist load reversal well since they rely on clamping friction rather than bearing/shear alone.

questions.text: If the thickness of a plate to be connected by a rivet is 16 mm, then suitable size of rivet as per Unwin's formula will be
questions.expl: Unwin's formula d = 6.04√t gives d = 6.04×√16 ≈ 24.2 mm, rounded to the next standard size of 27 mm.

questions.text: As compared to field rivets, shop rivets are
questions.expl: Shop rivets, driven under better controlled conditions, are stronger and more reliable than field-driven rivets.

questions.text: Bending compressive and tensile stresses respectively are calculated based on
options: Net area in both the cases
questions.expl: Bending compressive stress is calculated on gross section, while bending tensile stress is calculated on net section (accounting for holes).

questions.text: When two plates are placed end-to-end and are joined by two cover plates, the joint is known as
questions.expl: Two plates joined end-to-end using cover plates on both faces form a double-cover butt joint.

questions.text: The rivets subjected to unpredictable tension during the placement are
questions.expl: Hot-driven rivets develop unpredictable clamping tension as they cool and contract after installation.

questions.text: Load on connection is not eccentric for
options: Any of the joints mentioned above
questions.expl: A double-cover butt joint is symmetric about the main plate, so the load path has no eccentricity.

questions.text: Two steel plates, each of 12 mm thickness, are connected by a double-cover butt joint by bolts. If the bolt diameter is 20 mm and steel is Fe410, which section is most critical for a cover plate?
questions.expl: For the given cover plate geometry, section 1–1 (passing through the first row of bolt holes) has the least net area and governs.

questions.text: If the diameter of a bolt is 20 mm then the maximum number of bolt(s) that can be accommodated in one row in a 140 mm wide flat is (are)
questions.expl: With minimum pitch/edge distance requirements for 20 mm bolts, only 2 bolts fit within a 140 mm wide flat in one row.

questions.text: If the same number of bolts has been used in the joints, then which of the following patterns will yield highest efficiency?
questions.expl: A diamond (staggered, tapered) bolt pattern minimizes the reduction in net section at any one cross-section, giving the highest efficiency.

questions.text: A high strength bolt may be used for
questions.expl: High strength bolts (HSFG) can be designed either as slip-resistant (friction) connections or as bearing-type connections.

questions.text: The shear strength of long bolted joints is reduced by accounting for
questions.expl: Long joint reduction accounts specifically for overloading of end bolts due to uneven load sharing along the joint length (statement 1).

questions.text: The partial safety factor for the material of bolts is
questions.expl: IS:800 specifies the partial safety factor γmb for bolt material as 1.25.

questions.text: The shear strength of the bolt with threads intercepting the interface can be written as fs·An, where fs is given by
questions.expl: The nominal shear strength per unit area for such bolts is fu/√3 with the design factor 1.25 (relating to threaded shank area).

questions.text: The nominal tensile capacity of the bolt is given by
questions.expl: IS:800 gives the nominal tensile capacity of a bolt as Tnb = 0.9 fub Anb (before dividing by the partial safety factor for design capacity).

questions.text: Prying forces are the additional
options: Shearing forces on the bolts because of long joints
Bending forces on the bolts because of long joints
Tensile forces due to the flexibility of connected parts leading to deformations
Forces due to friction between the connected parts
questions.expl: Prying action induces extra tensile force in bolts due to flexing/deformation of the connected flange or plate under load.

questions.text: The tensile strength of the plate is given by
questions.expl: The design tensile (rupture) strength of the net section is 0.9 fu An divided by the partial safety factor γm1.

questions.text: The interaction equation for checking the bolts for combined shear and tension is
questions.expl: IS:800 uses a quadratic (elliptical) interaction formula: (Vsb/Vdb)² + (Tb/Tdb)² ≤ 1 for combined shear and tension in bolts.

questions.text: Proof stress for minimum bolt tension is given by
questions.expl: The minimum bolt pretension for HSFG bolts is specified as 0.70 times the ultimate tensile strength of the bolt material.

questions.text: Design of pins is primarily governed by
questions.expl: Pin connections are primarily designed for flexural (bending) stresses, since the pin spans between bearing surfaces like a small beam.

questions.text: ISHB stands for
questions.expl: ISHB denotes the Indian Standard Heavy (wide-flange) Beam series of rolled sections.

questions.text: Steel of yield strength 400 MPa has been used in a structure. What is the value of the maximum allowable strength?
questions.expl: Under WSM, permissible stress is typically taken as 0.6 fy = 0.6×400 = 240 MPa.

questions.text: Steel structures are ideally suitable for impact loads because they have high:
questions.expl: Structural steel has high toughness (ability to absorb energy before fracture), making it well suited to resist impact loading.

questions.text: According to IS:800-1962 the permissible bending stress in steel slab plates is
questions.expl: IS:800-1962 (WSM) specified a permissible bending stress of 1890 kg/cm² for steel slab base plates.

questions.text: The method of design of steel framework for greatest rigidity and economy in weight is known as
questions.expl: Fully rigid design, which maintains full moment continuity at joints, gives the greatest rigidity and can lead to economy in weight.

questions.text: The stress at which a material fractures under large number of reversals of stress is called
questions.expl: The endurance (fatigue) limit is the stress level below which a material can withstand an infinite number of stress reversals without fracture.

questions.text: Match List 1 (Type of stress) with List 2 (Allowable value): (i) Axial tension (ii) Bending tension (iii) Max shear stress (iv) Bearing stress
questions.expl: Axial tension = 0.6fy(3), Bending tension = 0.66fy(2), Max shear = 0.4fy(4), Bearing = 0.75fy(1), matching option B.

questions.text: Load factor is defined as
questions.expl: Load factor is the ratio of the ultimate (collapse) load capacity of a structure to its actual working load.

questions.text: The heaviest I-section for same depth is
questions.expl: For a given depth, ISHB (Heavy Beam) sections have the thickest flanges/webs, making them the heaviest among standard I-sections.

questions.text: Weight of steel per cubic metre is taken to be
questions.expl: The unit weight of structural steel is conventionally taken as about 7850–7900 kg/m³.

questions.text: The material cost of steel structures is usually about ____ of the total cost of the structure.
questions.expl: Material cost of steel typically forms about 30% of total steel structure cost, the rest being fabrication, erection and other costs.

questions.text: The life period of a steel commercial building is
questions.expl: Design life of a typical commercial steel building is conventionally taken as around 50 years.

questions.text: IS:800–2007 limits the values of width-to-thickness ratios of the elements of a steel section to place a check on
questions.expl: Width-to-thickness (b/t) ratio limits in IS:800:2007 classify sections and prevent premature local buckling of plate elements.

questions.text: For a combination of dead load and earthquake load, the partial safety factors for limit state of strength are respectively
questions.expl: For the DL + EL load combination, IS:800 assigns partial safety factors of 1.2 for both dead load and earthquake load.

questions.text: For checking the deflection of beams, the partial safety factors for dead load and live load would be
questions.expl: Serviceability (deflection) checks use unfactored (partial safety factor = 1) loads for both dead and live load.

questions.text: The partial safety factor for materials governed by buckling is
questions.expl: IS:800 specifies γm0 = 1.10 as the partial safety factor for buckling failure of structural steel members.

questions.text: Which of the following is not into a serviceability criteria?
questions.expl: Fatigue is a strength (ultimate) limit state concern, not a serviceability criterion like deflection, ponding, or vibration.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a limit state of strength?
questions.expl: Vibration is a serviceability limit state, not a strength limit state like fatigue fracture, brittle fracture, or rupture.

questions.text: Upper yield point in the stress-strain curve in structural steel can be avoided by
questions.expl: Cold working of steel removes the distinct upper yield point observed in the stress-strain curve of as-rolled (hot-worked) steel.

questions.text: The permissible tensile stress in a steel member is given by
questions.expl: Under the Working Stress Method, permissible axial tensile stress is conventionally taken as 0.6fy.

questions.text: A tension member, if subjected to possible reversal of stress due to wind, the slenderness ratio of the member should not exceed
questions.expl: Tension members subject to stress reversal from wind/seismic action are limited to a maximum slenderness ratio of 350.

questions.text: According to IS:800–1984, the permissible stress in axial tension in steel is [fy = minimum yield stress]
questions.expl: IS:800-1984 (WSM) specifies the permissible axial tensile stress as 0.6 times the yield stress.

questions.text: When the secondary stresses are taken into account along with primary stresses then the allowable stress is increased by
questions.expl: IS:800 permits a 33⅓% increase in allowable stress when secondary stresses are combined with primary stresses.

questions.text: In a tension member, when one or more than one rivet hole is off the line, then the failure of the plate depends upon
questions.expl: For a staggered (zig-zag) failure path, the net section depends on hole diameter, pitch, and gauge — all these factors together.

questions.text: The net sectional area of a tension member is equal to
options: Gross sectional area minus the maximum deduction for rivet holes
Gross sectional area plus maximum deduction for rivet holes
Two times the gross sectional area
questions.expl: Net area is the gross area reduced by subtracting the maximum area lost to rivet/bolt holes along the critical failure path.

questions.text: A structural member subjected to tensile force in the direction parallel to its longitudinal axis is called
options: A tension member or a tie
questions.expl: A member carrying axial tension along its longitudinal axis is termed a tension member or tie.

questions.text: In a structure generally wires and cables are used as
questions.expl: Wires and cables have negligible flexural or compressive stiffness and can only usefully carry tensile forces.

questions.text: Ties are load carrying members of a frame which are subjected to
questions.expl: A tie, by definition, is a member designed to carry purely axial tensile load.

questions.text: The net effective cross sectional area calculated in the steel angle tension member design, accounts for
options: The tensile force and bolts holes
The eccentricity of the end connections and the bolt holes
The effectiveness of the tack connection along the length
The effectiveness of the end connection
questions.expl: The effective net area formula for angle sections accounts for both the eccentricity of end connections and the deduction for bolt holes.

questions.text: A steel plate is 30 cm wide and 10 mm thick. A rivet of nominal diameter 18 mm is driven. The net sectional area of the plate is
questions.expl: Gross diameter = 18+1.5=19.5mm; Net area = (300−19.5)×10 = 2805 mm² = 28.05 cm².

questions.text: The best tension member section will be a
options: Double-angle section on opposite side of gusset plate
questions.expl: A double-angle section placed symmetrically on opposite sides of a gusset plate avoids eccentricity, making it the most efficient tension member.

questions.text: What is the effective net width of the plate for carrying tension? (Holes dia 25mm; plate 300mm wide; edge offsets 50 & 100mm; gauge 40 & 50mm)
questions.expl: The effective net width is obtained by deducting hole diameters and adding staggered pitch corrections (p²/4g terms) per IS:800, giving 237.5 mm here.

questions.text: A tension member splice is designed for
options: Maximum of factored tensile force or 0.3 times the design strength of the member
Maximum of compressive or tensile force in the member
questions.expl: IS:800 requires splices to be designed for the greater of the actual factored force or a minimum of 0.3 times the member's design strength.

questions.text: In case of angle section lug angles, their attachment to the member should be capable of developing x% in excess of the force in outstanding leg of the angle, where x is
questions.expl: Lug angle connections must be designed to develop 40% in excess of the force carried by the outstanding leg.

questions.text: The unstiffened top edge of a gusset plate (fy = 250 MPa) should be limited to
questions.expl: For fy = 250 MPa, IS:800 limits the unstiffened free edge of a gusset plate to 42 times its thickness.

questions.text: A gusset plate is subjected to
questions.expl: A gusset plate transferring forces between multiple members experiences a combination of direct, shear and bending stresses.

questions.text: The design tensile strength of a member due to yielding of gross section Tdg is given by
questions.expl: Design strength governed by yielding of the gross section is Tdg = Ag fy / γm0.

questions.text: The design tensile strength of a plate due to rupture of critical section is given by
questions.expl: Design strength governed by rupture of the net section is Tdn = 0.9 An fu / γm1.

questions.text: A fillet weld is known as standard fillet weld if the cross section of the fillet weld is triangle of the angle of
questions.expl: A standard fillet weld has a cross-section forming a right-angled isosceles triangle, i.e., 45° angle on each leg.

questions.text: A butt weld is specified by
questions.expl: Butt welds are specified in terms of their effective throat thickness, unlike fillet welds specified by leg size.

questions.text: Which of the following does not describe a weld type?
questions.expl: 'Zigzag weld' is not a standard weld type classification (butt, plug, fillet, lap/slot are standard types).

questions.text: A plate used for connecting two or more structural members intersecting each other is called
questions.expl: A gusset plate is used to connect two or more intersecting structural members at a joint.

questions.text: The effective length of a fillet weld of length ℓ is
questions.expl: The effective length of a fillet weld deducts twice the weld size from its overall length: L − 2s.

questions.text: Welded connections are preferred to riveted connection because
options: The loss of member strength is smaller
questions.expl: Welded connections generally reduce material and labor requirements compared to riveting, making them more economical.

questions.text: As compared to riveting, welding is preferred these days because
questions.expl: Welding is preferred over riveting for being quieter, more economical, and achieving higher joint efficiency — all correct.

questions.text: The effective length of the fillet weld is
questions.expl: Effective length of a fillet weld equals its overall (total) length minus twice the weld (leg) size.

questions.text: The actual thickness of butt weld as compared to thickness of plate is usually
questions.expl: Butt welds are usually built up slightly thicker than the plate (with reinforcement) to ensure full strength development.

questions.text: For a standard 45° fillet, the ratio of size of fillet to throat thickness is
questions.expl: For a standard 45° fillet weld, throat thickness = 0.707×size, so the ratio of size to throat is √2:1.

questions.text: The effective length of a fillet weld should not be less than
questions.expl: IS:800 requires the effective length of a fillet weld to be at least 4 times its size, per some codal statements minimum length is taken as 6 times the weld size for effectiveness in this reference.

questions.text: In the cross-section of a weld, the throat is the
questions.expl: The throat thickness of a fillet weld is its minimum (critical) dimension, used to determine its design strength.

questions.text: Which one of the following is the mode of failure in a fillet weld material?
questions.expl: Fillet weld material is assumed to fail in shear across its throat section under design loads.

questions.text: For two plates of equal thickness, full strength of fillet weld can be ensured if its maximum size, for square edge, is limited to
questions.expl: For a square-edged plate, the maximum fillet weld size is limited to 1.5 mm less than the plate thickness to avoid edge melt-through.

questions.text: Spot welding is used when two plates are placed
options: At right angles to each other
questions.expl: Spot welding joins two overlapping plates placed one on top of the other by fusing them at discrete spot locations.

questions.text: The design nominal strength of a fillet weld is
questions.expl: The nominal shear strength of fillet weld metal is taken as fu/√3, based on the ultimate strength of the weaker connected part.

questions.text: The design capacity of a weld is reduced when the length of welded joint is greater than
questions.expl: IS:800 requires a reduction in design strength for long welded lap joints when the joint length exceeds 150 times the weld throat thickness.

questions.text: The imperfection factor for welded steel sections is
questions.expl: IS:800 assigns a higher imperfection factor (α = 0.49, buckling curve 'c' or 'd') to welded built-up sections due to residual stresses.
